focus: Family 139 transfer to Bayesian kinetic posteriors: explicit affine negative-curvature counterexample plus an exactly eligible coupled two-state binding-assay family; N68 retained only as concise negative appendix.

source_snapshot.manuscript: Subpolynomial query complexity for well-conditioned log-concave sampling

claims.statement: For d>=2 and every fixed epsilon>0, the pinned manuscript claims a measurable randomized algorithm with at most C_epsilon*d^epsilon exact adaptive value-and-gradient queries on every execution and TV error at most 1/10, uniformly for C^2 V on R^d with V(0)=0, grad V(0)=0, and I<=Hess V(x)<=2I globally. It also claims Q(d)>=c log d for sufficiently large d, including centered Gaussian quadratics.
assumptions: Exact real value-and-gradient oracle is the algorithm's only information about V
Origin is a supplied minimizer
Random real variables and unrestricted computation are allowed
Fixed positive epsilon; C_epsilon may depend on epsilon
claims.status: source-reported theorem; exact interface reconstructed from primary manuscript; full proof not independently audited in this workstream
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Pinned theorem and exact oracle contract'; pinned manuscript Sections 1.1 and 8-9, Theorems 1.1, 8.5, 9.1
claims.novelty_boundary: No claim of polylogarithmic queries, finite-bit complexity, practical runtime, or theorem transfer to non-log-concave posteriors.

costs.oracle: One exact (V(x), grad V(x)) response per query; worst-execution cap C_epsilon*d^epsilon.
costs.supplied: Known minimizer at zero and normalized potential.
costs.computation: Unrestricted between queries; no arithmetic or bit-complexity guarantee.

claims.falsifier: A counterexample inside the exact oracle class or a verified flaw in the primary proof.
claims.next_gate: Independent full proof audit and a finite-representation/runtime accounting if used computationally.

claims.statement: If a transformed enzyme posterior potential U has supplied mode z_star and a supplied/proved SPD G satisfying G<=Hess U(z)<=2G for all z, then P=G^(-1/2), V(x)=U(z_star+P*x)-U(z_star) satisfy the family-139 normalization and Hessian bounds. Running the released sampler and mapping back preserves TV error.
assumptions: Posterior density is proper and twice differentiable in declared coordinates
Correct change-of-measure Jacobian is included
A global Hessian sandwich and exact transformed mode are supplied/proved
Exact deterministic value-and-gradient oracle is available
claims.status: conditional derivation; algebraic congruence and TV invariance checked
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Conditional map from an enzyme posterior'
claims.novelty_boundary: Does not show real enzyme posteriors satisfy the global sandwich or supply mode/preconditioner acquisition.

costs.queries: C_epsilon*d^epsilon exact transformed value-gradient calls for each fixed epsilon.
costs.outside_theorem: Data acquisition, mode finding, G selection/certification, ODE solves, adjoints, arithmetic, and bit precision are uncharged by the theorem.
costs.map: The posterior-to-V mapping is a bijection, so TV distance is unchanged.

claims.falsifier: Failure of global G<=Hess U<=2G, failure of a proper smooth posterior density, or non-exact/non-integrable oracle responses.
claims.next_gate: For a fixed assay and prior, provide or refute a global curvature certificate after the exact declared coordinate transformation.

claims.statement: For the two-parameter Michaelis-Menten rate posterior with mu=exp(psi)/(1+exp(phi)), y=1/10, sigma=1/10, and independent N(0,10^2) priors on log parameters (phi,psi), U_phi_phi(-log 3,0)=-4109/1600<0. Consequently no translation and invertible affine preconditioner can place this posterior in the family-139 Hessian class.
assumptions: E_T=S=1
Gaussian observation likelihood with standard deviation 0.1
Independent Gaussian log-parameter priors with standard deviation 10
Potential defined with respect to log-coordinate Lebesgue measure
claims.status: internally derived exact counterexample; arithmetic checked; not an experimental dataset
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Worked enzyme-kinetic counterexample to the affine bridge'
claims.novelty_boundary: Refutes the general log-transform plus affine-whitening transfer, not every enzyme posterior or every nonlinear coordinate map.

costs.data: One synthetic rate datum and specified Gaussian error.
costs.prior: Proper 2D Gaussian prior in log-parameter coordinates.

claims.falsifier: An arithmetic error in the displayed derivative or a violation of Sylvester's law for the stated invertible affine maps.
claims.next_gate: Try a precisely specified nonlinear coordinate transform only if its correct density Jacobian and global Hessian bounds can be certified.

claims.statement: For a two-state logistic binding assay with z~N(0,I), design rows b_j, and one bound plus one unbound observation per setting, the transformed posterior potential V(z)=0.5||z||^2+2*sum_j log cosh(b_j^T z/2) has mode zero and Hessian I+0.5 B^T diag(sech^2(Bz/2))B. If B^T B<=2I globally, then I<=Hess V<=2I and family 139 applies. A sparse coupled design B_d=[I_d; C_d/2], where C_d has adjacent-sum rows e_k+e_(k+1), satisfies this condition for every d>=2.
assumptions: Binary observations follow the exact two-state equilibrium/logistic occupancy model
Gaussian prior is whitened to N(0,I)
Each setting has exactly one bound and one unbound replicate
Assay log-odds are centered at the prior mean and are linear in z
Known design satisfies B^T B<=2I
claims.status: conditional model theorem derived exactly; not an observed experimental dataset; balanced high-dimensional data can be rare
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Positive capability path: an exactly checkable two-state binding assay'
claims.novelty_boundary: A constructed idealized equilibrium binding/occupancy observation family only; not a general enzyme-turnover, Michaelis-Menten trajectory, or cell-signaling posterior, and no practical advantage or experiment is claimed.

costs.posterior_queries: At most C_epsilon*d^epsilon exact value-gradient queries on every execution for each fixed epsilon, with TV error at most 0.1.
costs.data: For the sparse coupled design, m=2d-1 settings and 4d-2 binary outcomes; all paired data, prior parameters, and design coefficients must be supplied.
costs.data_rarity: Under z=0, probability all m independent pairs are balanced is 2^(-m).
costs.oracle_evaluation: Sparse B_d permits O(d) real arithmetic per explicit value-gradient evaluation; family 139 does not bound its own between-query computation or finite precision.
costs.outside_theorem: Assay acquisition, calibration, preprocessing, physical noise, and runtime/bit costs are additional.

claims.falsifier: A violation of the displayed logistic likelihood, exact score cancellation, the Hessian identity, or the spectral inequality for B_d.
claims.next_gate: Test a realistic binding assay with measured design coefficients and data; certify balanced-score/mode and global spectral curvature, then compare matched HMC/MALA wall-clock and posterior error.

claims.statement: Primary applied systems-biology literature uses parallel tempering for Bayesian kinetic parameter estimation; in one synthetic Michaelis-Menten experiment it reports mean convergence thresholds of 369 four-chain PT steps versus 4203 MH steps, and in a 12-parameter calcium-signaling example only a fraction of chains converge within 500000 steps.
assumptions: Reported synthetic models, initializations, noise, convergence criteria, and implementation in Gupta et al. 2018
claims.status: source-reported empirical primary prior art; not reproduced here and not a general guarantee
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Primary prior art and equally informed controls'; Gupta et al. HTML lines 161-197
claims.novelty_boundary: Specific finite empirical comparisons only; no novelty or universal superiority claim.

costs.comparison: Four model integrations per reported PT step; approximately 1476 integrations for 369 steps versus 4203 MH integrations to their convergence threshold.
costs.limitation: Synthetic data and convergence-threshold metric; posterior-sample error not certified.

claims.falsifier: A mismatch with the cited article's methods/results or a controlled reproduction yielding materially different counts.
claims.next_gate: On a fixed assay, compare effective sample quality per forward/adjoint model solve against PT with matched data, priors, and target.

claims.statement: The N68 algebraic full-matrix output cannot directly equal a finite-dimensional unitary pulse channel or CPTP evolution map in the n=s=1 instance, because its prescribed matrix has eigenvalue 2 while these channel maps have spectral radius at most 1.
assumptions: Direct identification up to similarity
N68's card-stated query matrix and exact output interface
claims.status: concise card-derived negative appendix; proof files cited by the card were absent from the pinned tree in earlier retrieval; no independent theorem audit
claims.novelty_boundary: Rules out direct physical-map identity only; indirect encodings and experimental realizations remain unresolved.

costs.algebraic_query: One exact full matrix in dimension 2s; full response rational bit length charged.
costs.physical_query: Ordinary pulse-channel identification is shot-noisy and has a different output interface.

claims.falsifier: A legal direct finite-dimensional channel realization with the same spectrum up to similarity.
claims.next_gate: None in this workstream after parent redirection; any indirect realization requires a separately specified encoded interface.

baseline.statement: Smoothed Picard HMC is a close primary classical gradient-query predecessor under strong-convexity/smoothness assumptions, with a d^(1/6)-type fixed-accuracy Wasserstein query dependence and a distinct high-accuracy TV theorem. It does not apply to the explicit negative-curvature posterior.
baseline.statement_applied: Parallel tempering is the information-matched applied baseline for the stated nonconvex kinetic posterior; source-reported comparisons count model integrations, unlike the abstract exact-oracle theorem.

evidence_boundary: Source-derived/conditional only. No independent proof audit, external theorem validation, experiment, or novelty/priority claim.
